properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-25, answering `quality_target_unstated` on reflow2's own design and pointing at the project's own elevator-speech summary as the source.

═══ THE SENTENCE THE ANSWER COMES FROM ═══

*"It reports rather than judges, and it refuses to guess. It will tell you a boundary is undeclared; it won't invent the contract. It will tell you a part holds no function; it won't decide what belongs there. Absence is recorded as absence — 'nobody was asked' never gets rounded up to 'answered.'"*

That is a claim about one thing: **whether the state of the design can be correctly determined from what reflow2 says about it.** That is observability, in its precise sense — not logging, but the property that outputs do not misrepresent internal state.

═══ WHY THIS AXIS AND NOT ANOTHER ═══

The cardinal sin in this project is a **green gate over ground it never covered**, and the whole vocabulary is built to prevent it: `loop_status` REFUSES an unknown contributor rather than answering "nothing is owed to you"; `evaluate_allocation` reports `modularity: null` instead of the meaningless 1.00 it used to; `Decision.no_relation_note` exists because prose cannot be told apart from silence; `Capability.delivery` and `Decision.quality_target` carry NO DEFAULT so absence reads as "nobody said"; `detect_gaps` says what it withheld; `scan_nodes` reports `omitted`. Every one of those is the same trade being made the same way, and none of them buys speed, safety or scale.

⚠️ MAINTAINABILITY WAS THE RUNNER-UP AND THE MEASUREMENT ARGUES AGAINST IT. The product exists so a design survives change, which sounds like maintainability — but that axis wants what changes together to live together, and reflow2's own co-change experiment (2026-08-21) measured **71% of its strongest co-change signal crossing its subsystem boundaries**. Its decomposition is functional (`dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`), not co-change-optimal. Claiming maintainability would assert a target its own structure demonstrably does not serve.

PERFORMANCE, SCALABILITY AND SECURITY are not close. It is a single-user design tool over one graph per project; latency is not what anyone judges it on, and the design holds ONE weighted coupling edge in 211 capabilities — nobody has ever optimised chatter here.

═══ WHAT THIS SHAPES ═══

Observability-driven allocation wants the INSTRUMENT SEPARATED FROM THE SUBJECT, so a part can report on another part without being able to quietly flatter it — and that is already the shape: detection (`sys:coherence-loop`) is a separate subsystem from the store it reads, and reporting is separate from the graph it summarises. The rule this makes binding on future work: **a part that reports on something must be able to say it could not tell**, and any new detector owes an answer for the case where it had nothing to run on.

📌 RECORDED WITH ITS PROVENANCE BECAUSE THE AXIS CALL WAS THE AGENT'S READING of the user's own summary, not the user's word for word. He supplied the source and directed that it be recorded; the choice among nine axes is argued above and is overturnable with a single `set_quality_target` call.
properties.name: DECIDED — reflow2 is built for OBSERVABILITY: its answers must never misrepresent what it knows
properties.rationale:
The first answer to `quality_target_unstated` on reflow2's own design, five hours after the detector that asks it was built — `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches`, closed in the same session for once.

Recorded as an accepted Decision rather than left proposed because the owner supplied the source and asked for it to be populated. The reasoning for the specific axis is written out in full precisely because it was a judgement made from his summary rather than a word he said, so overturning it costs one call and loses nothing.
